newsitem.title: GERMANY: German MGM media firm develops new online ad plan.
newsitem.headline: German MGM media firm develops new online ad plan.

text.p: German television marketing agency MediaGruppe Muenchen (MGM) said on Thursday it would only charge online advertisers when adverts reached their target groups in order to help reduce doubts about the medium.

By counting the number of mouse clicks on an advertisers' Web site and looking at compiled user data, MGM said it could tell advertisers who had visited their site and how intensely they had investigated it and then bill companies accordingly.

"The goal of the new MGM-model is the faster development and establishment of online advertising," MGM said in a statement. "With it, the risks of the new medium as a space for advertising do not have to be carried by an advertiser alone."

When users click on a company's advert with a mouse, this so-called AdClick costs advertisers two marks. MGM said this system allowed it to weed out users who happened to surf by and only count those who spent time actually looking at the site.

The agency said AdClicks were an improvement on the current industry standard of counting "Page Views" and "Visits", adopted to measure online advertising impact by German Association of Newspaper Publishers (VDZ) for a recent report.

While counting Page Views and Visits only told if a page of an Web site had been opened, MGM said monitoring the number of times a user clicked on parts of a site gave it a clearer picture of his or her level of interest in its content.

MGM said still aenemic investment in cyberspace advertising in Germany showed clients' persistent jitters. German advertisers spent only five million marks on online adverts last year versus $300 million in the United States.
